ap_chemistry-m01.stem: The reaction A(g) + B(g) ⇌ C(g) is at equilibrium in a closed container at constant temperature, with [A] = 0.5 M, [B] = 0.2 M, and [C] = 0.4 M and Kc = 4. The volume of the container is suddenly increased to twice its original value, and the temperature does not change. Which statement correctly compares the reaction quotient Q with Kc immediately after the change and gives the direction of the shift?

options.text: Q = 8 is larger than Kc = 4, so the net reaction shifts toward the reactant, the side with more gas molecules.
options.why: Every concentration is multiplied by 0.5, so Q = 8 against Kc = 4 gives Q/Kc = 2; Q is larger than Kc, so the net change moves toward the reactant, which is the side with more moles of gas.

options.text: Q = 2 is smaller than Kc = 4, so the net reaction shifts toward the product until Q equals Kc again.
options.why: Assumes Q scales linearly with the concentration change and ignores the exponents, so both the value and the direction come out wrong.

options.text: Q is still equal to Kc = 4 because Kc depends only on temperature, so the mixture stays at equilibrium and there is no shift.
options.why: Believes that a constant K means Q cannot change, so volume changes cause no shift.

options.text: Q = 8 is larger than Kc = 4, so the net reaction shifts toward the product, the side with fewer gas molecules, until Q equals Kc.
options.why: Reads Q > K backward and picks the opposite direction.

ap_chemistry-m02.stem: At a certain temperature the reaction A(g) ⇌ B(g) + C(g) has Kc = 6.4×10⁻⁹. A closed container starts with [A] = 0.1 M and no B or C. Which statement gives the equilibrium concentration of B and a correct reason the simplification used to find it is valid?

options.text: [B] ≈ 5.1×10⁻⁵ M, found from the same simplified expression after multiplying x by 2 although B has a coefficient of 1, which is valid because Kc is so small.
options.why: Mishandles the coefficient when converting the change x into the equilibrium concentration.

options.text: [B] ≈ 8.0×10⁻⁵ M, found by taking the square root of Kc alone, which is valid because Kc is so small that the initial concentration does not matter.
options.why: Drops the initial concentration from the expression, treating the square root of Kc as the answer.

options.text: [B] ≈ 2.5×10⁻⁵ M, found from Kc = x²/(0.1 − x) ≈ x²/0.1, which is valid because x is only about 0.025% of the initial concentration.
options.why: With x as the change, Kc = x²/(0.1 − x) ≈ x²/0.1 gives x ≈ 2.5×10⁻⁵ M (the quadratic gives 2.5×10⁻⁵ M, the same to two figures), so [B] = x = 2.5×10⁻⁵ M; x is 0.0253% of 0.1 M, below the 5% rule, so dropping x from the subtraction is justified.

options.text: [B] ≈ 6.4×10⁻⁹ M, because a very small Kc means the equilibrium concentration of the product is approximately equal to Kc itself.
options.why: Treats the numerical value of Kc as a concentration instead of a ratio of concentrations.
